html:
Yamaye was the Taino name for the island of Jamaica, and the Yamayeka were its people. They were Arawakan-speaking farmers who grew cassava and sweet potato in mounded fields, fished, and lived in villages under chiefs, called caciques.

Columbus reached the island in 1494, on his second voyage, and in 1503 to 1504 he was stranded there for a year on his fourth. Spanish settlement began in 1509 at Sevilla la Nueva on the north coast. Forced labour and new diseases destroyed the Taino of Jamaica within a few decades, and the Spanish brought enslaved Africans in their place. The English took the island from Spain in 1655; see Jamaica.
